relations.subject: sgw:channel-cmd
relations.evidence: Every document processed by the Sync Gateway is assigned to a channel (user-defined or system-defined). A channel is the fundamental way to segregate documents and for enforcing access control.

relations.subject: sgw:user
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - established for sgw:role in roles.json (role granted access to zero-or-more channels); same shape applies directly to a user
relations.evidence: Every Sync Gateway user is granted access to zero, one or more channels.

relations.subject: sgw:role
relations.evidence: A Sync Gateway role is a way of logically grouping users. Like the channel, a role is granted access to zero, one or more channels.

relations.subject: sgw:user
relations.evidence: Users can also be assigned to zero or more Roles.

relations.subject: sgw:user
relations.evidence: A user inherits the channel access of all roles it belongs to. This is very much like Unix groups, except that roles do not form a hierarchy.

relations.subject: sgw:user
relations.evidence: Sync Gateway users and roles have no relationship to Couchbase Server's RBAC (Role-based Access Control) users. They are created and operate solely within the Sync Gateway ecosphere to govern access to replication data and to the Public API.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - the default (un-customized) sync function's specific behavior of naming the implicit channel after the collection; distinct from the generic scopedToCollection relation already captured in sync-function.json
relations.evidence: By default, every document in the collection is automatically assigned to a channel with the same name as the collection. This system automatically creates a channel with the collection's name.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-access-revocation
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused (behavesDifferentlyUnder is a promoted relation) - used here for its intended purpose: the same feature (revocation) has a materially different effect depending on SGW major version
relations.evidence:
3.0 Breaking Change

Whenever a user loses access to a channel (or channels) all document in the channel(s) are auto-purged from local Couchbase Lite databases.
In Sync Gateway 2.x these documents remain in the local database on channel access loss.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-access-revocation
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - captures that role membership changes are one of several distinct triggers for revocation, alongside direct channel removal; no equivalent 'cascading revocation cause' concept exists in server/'s or Capella's static grant models
relations.evidence: Users may lose access to documents for many reasons, including: The User loses direct access to channel; The User is removed from a role; A role the user belongs to is revoked access to channel.

relations.subject: sgw:public-channel
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - an automatic, unconditional grant with no analogue in server/'s privilege model (every privilege must be explicitly assigned) or Capella's role model
relations.evidence: Documents assigned to this channel can be accessed by all users; even users assigned no specific channel access. New users are automatically granted access to the channel.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-cmd
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - same predicate as the generic channel-routing relation, applied to the named system channel
relations.evidence: You assign a document to the public (!) channel using the channel() function.

relations.subject: sgw:all-documents-channel
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - the source text issues an explicit non-conflation warning between two lookalike ('*') concepts, a stronger claim than a generic seeAlso cross-reference
relations.evidence: This channel should not be confused with the use of the All Channels Wildcard in access grants.

relations.subject: sgw:all-channels-wildcard
relations.evidence: The All Channels Wildcard ('*') — used when granting user access, this wildcard grants access to any document in any channel.

relations.subject: sgw:all-channels-wildcard
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - captures a subtle asymmetry: holding the wildcard grant does not satisfy a requireAccess() check for any specific named channel, unlike a direct channel grant which does; no such asymmetry exists between a fixed privilege and a role that includes it in server/'s or Capella's models
relations.evidence: Users granted access using the all channels wildcard do not inherit requireAccess() rights to any specific channel.

relations.subject: sgw:admin-rest-api
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - ties a provisioning surface to the specific field it can write, a level of granularity server/'s single named-privilege list never needs (there the surface IS the grant)
relations.evidence: Using the Admin REST API: You can provide the admin_channels property within the collection_access property using the Admin REST API endpoint.

relations.subject: sgw:admin-channels-property
relations.evidence: the channels topic discusses how channels are created and how documents can be assigned to channels

relations.subject: sgw:legacy-pre-3-config
relations.evidence: File-based Configuration Properties: This is only available in 3.x and is typically used for dev/test environments. You can do it in the Sync Gateway JSON Configuration File... by adding the appropriate channel to the user's admin_channels property.

cross_product_finding: This page is the fullest single statement of the SGW access-control shape in this batch, and it confirms requiresPrivilege does not generalize here at all. server/'s model is: operation -> checked against -> one named privilege from a fixed, product-defined enum. Capella's model is: API call -> checked against -> one management-plane role from a fixed enum, keyed additionally by credential type. SGW's model inverts the direction of the check entirely: there is no 'operation requires X' lookup. Instead, (1) every document is TAGGED with one or more channels by application-authored JavaScript (the sync function), (2) every user/role is independently GRANTED membership in zero-or-more channels (also often via that same JavaScript, or via a REST property), and (3) a read succeeds purely from set-intersection between a document's channels and a user's (possibly role-inherited) channels - there is no operation-specific gate at all for reads. Write/delete access is the ONLY place anything resembling requiresPrivilege appears, and even there it is opt-in, ad hoc application logic (requireUser/requireRole/requireAccess calls the docs author writes into their own sync function) rather than a platform-enforced, declared requirement - the platform provides the helper functions, but nothing forces a sync function to call them, and a sync function that never calls them has no write restrictions at all. Additionally, SGW layers in behavior with zero counterpart in server/ or Capella: (a) a replicated-client cache invalidation problem (channel access revocation causing auto-purge on Couchbase Lite, versioned differently across 2.x vs 3.0 - see behavesDifferentlyUnder), and (b) automatic/implicit grants (the public channel, the all-documents channel) that are unconditional rather than assigned. Finally, this page reinforces (already seen in users.json) that SGW deliberately runs a SECOND, disjoint, server/-native RBAC system (sgw:rbac-user) purely to gate its own Admin/Metrics API - meaning a single Sync Gateway deployment straddles both prior batches' models simultaneously, just for different API surfaces of the same product.
